# Toy MIDI

> Toy MIDI is a browser-based DAW for editing MIDI and recording audio. This guide is for agents. It explains the two ways an agent can work with a project: driving the app open in the user's browser, or writing a share link that opens a song in the app.

Projects live in the browser's own storage. The app has no server, no accounts, and no API to call over HTTP. Its pages are:

- `/`, the project list.
- `/recorder/<projectId>`, a project saved in this browser.
- `/draft#p=<payload>`, a project carried in a share link. It opens unsaved, so the person who opens it can edit it and then save their own copy.

Links and pages are on the site that served this guide.

## Choose How to Work

Drive the open app when you need to listen and revise. You can play, seek, and loop the project and hear what you changed, which is how arrangement and mixing work gets done.

Write a share link when you cannot reach the user's browser, such as from a remote or cloud session, or when you are composing and the user will tell you what they think in words. You write the project as JSON, encode it into a link, and post the link.

## Drive the Open App

The app registers its tools with [WebMCP](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/), a proposed browser API for agents, through `document.modelContext`. The runtime the tools act on is declared in [`/llms/toy-midi.d.ts`](/llms/toy-midi.d.ts), so you can read it before you reach the page.

A browser or agent that supports WebMCP calls the tool directly. From a terminal, use [webmcp-bridge](https://github.com/hi-ogawa/toy-midi/tree/main/packages/webmcp-bridge), which connects you to a page open in the user's browser on the same machine. Install the command:

```sh
pnpm i -g "github:hi-ogawa/toy-midi#path:/packages/webmcp-bridge"
```

Then run `webmcp-bridge --help`, which covers connecting to the user's page and reading the tools it exposes. The user installs the extension once, following the package's README.

## Write a Share Link

A share link is the site's `/draft` page with the project in the URL fragment:

```
<site>/draft#p=<payload>
```

The payload is the project's saved format as JSON, compressed with raw deflate, without a zlib header, and encoded as base64url. The format's type is `SerializedEditorRuntimeState` in [`/llms/toy-midi.d.ts`](/llms/toy-midi.d.ts). Its optional fields fill in defaults when the project loads.

A link leaves out audio. Leave `audioTracks` empty, since audio samples need storage a link does not have. Ids need only be unique, tracks within the project and notes within their track, so short ones such as `"n1"` work and keep the link shorter.

Encode the payload with Node, which has raw deflate and base64url built in:

```js
import { deflateRawSync } from "node:zlib";

const payload = deflateRawSync(JSON.stringify(project)).toString("base64url");
```

Keep links short where they will be posted. A chat message can cap far below what a browser accepts, such as 2,000 characters on Discord, so a short phrase fits where a whole song may not.
